segments.name: Memecoin Markets
segments.intro: We begin with memecoins, speculative digital tokens often based on internet jokes or personalities.

stories.headline: Pump.fun criticized over data on token creators' earnings
stories.script_text: The memecoin launch platform Pump.fun is facing criticism online after figures circulated suggesting its most active token creators have earned large sums while most tokens lose nearly all their value. According to the figures, shared by several crypto commentators, the top twenty-five creators launched about seven hundred and seventy thousand tokens and earned roughly one hundred and twenty-eight million dollars. Only six of those tokens reached a market value of twenty million dollars. Some users are calling for a boycott. A widely shared quote attributing the criticism to Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin could not be traced to any original statement.

stories.headline: Pump.fun lets new tokens trade against any token launched on the platform
stories.script_text: Pump.fun also announced a change to how new tokens trade. Creators can now pair a new token against any token already launched on the platform, rather than only a short list of approved assets. The company says purchases of a new token will be routed through the token it is paired with, adding demand for that token. Pump.fun's own token, PUMP, was down about eleven per cent over the past day, according to CoinGecko.

stories.headline: Newly launched Solana tokens post extreme price swings
stories.script_text: Trading data show the extreme volatility of newly created tokens on the Solana blockchain. According to the market-data site GeckoTerminal, a token called TikTok, created just before noon Pacific time today, has risen more than sixteen hundred per cent, to a market value of about six hundred and eighty thousand dollars. Another, BORDR, is up about seventeen hundred per cent. A third, swordinu, traded about five million dollars' worth in a day and has lost ninety-nine point nine per cent of its value. Separately, a token called TWEETCRAFT doubled in price after dozens of accounts posted near-identical promotional messages, a pattern often associated with co-ordinated promotion.

stories.headline: Trader reports $4M wallet theft in Singapore; BNB Chain project loses $12.5M
stories.script_text: Two security incidents are drawing attention. A cryptocurrency trader known online as Frogman says about four million dollars was taken from two of his digital wallets in the early morning during the TOKEN2049 industry conference in Singapore. He says the funds were then moved through privacy services that make them harder to trace. Separately, on the BNB Chain network, an administrator account for a project called 79thVault used special permissions to withdraw about twelve and a half million dollars from a trading pool. Negotiations over a reward for returning the funds are reported to be under way.

stories.headline: High-risk trader returns with large leveraged Bitcoin bet
stories.script_text: A trader known as AguilaTrades has placed a forty-times-leveraged bet on Bitcoin that would be forcibly closed near eighty-one thousand five hundred dollars. Bitcoin is currently near {{BTC_PRICE}} dollars.

segments.name: Crypto Markets and Policy
segments.intro: Turning now to the wider cryptocurrency market.

stories.headline: Crypto markets: Bitcoin near {{BTC_PRICE_DIGITS}}
stories.script_text: As of {{PRICES_AS_OF_SPOKEN}}, Bitcoin was near {{BTC_PRICE}} U.S. dollars, {{BTC_CHANGE_SPOKEN}} over twenty-four hours. Ether was near {{ETH_PRICE}} dollars, {{ETH_CHANGE_SPOKEN}}, and Solana near {{SOL_PRICE}}, {{SOL_CHANGE_SPOKEN}}. More than a billion dollars in leveraged trades were forcibly closed earlier today.

stories.headline: Bitcoin funds see largest daily withdrawals in months
stories.script_text: Investors pulled about four hundred and eighty-five million dollars from U.S. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds on Tuesday, October seventh, according to data from Farside Investors. These funds trade on stock exchanges and hold Bitcoin directly. BlackRock's fund accounted for about two hundred and eight million dollars of the outflow. It was the largest single day of withdrawals in months.

stories.headline: EU regulator orders phase-out of non-compliant stablecoins, including USDT
stories.script_text: The European Union's markets regulator has told licensed crypto firms to phase out stablecoins that do not meet EU rules, including Tether's USDT, by January eighth, twenty twenty-seven.

stories.headline: U.S. CFTC proceeds with crypto trading rules
stories.script_text: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is proceeding with its own crypto trading rules while legislation stalls in Congress.

stories.headline: Strategy and Cardone Capital add to Bitcoin holdings
stories.script_text: Strategy now holds a record eight hundred and forty-eight thousand bitcoin, and Cardone Capital bought forty more today.

segments.name: Emerging Trends
segments.intro: Finally, a look at the themes shaping speculative trading this week.

stories.headline: Tokens based on AI-generated characters draw traders
stories.script_text: Tokens based on AI-generated characters, including Frank Ashford and Jean Phil, are among the most actively traded on Solana this week.

stories.headline: Tokens linked to company shares gain attention
stories.script_text: Tokens linked to company shares are gaining attention. Base network lead Jesse Pollak called tokenized shares the industry's next major growth area.

stories.headline: Research report on AI agents lifts Derive token
stories.script_text: A Citrini Research report on AI agents and crypto helped lift Derive's token about twenty-four per cent today.

stories.headline: Interest grows in memecoins that share revenue
stories.script_text: Injective's community fund bought ten per cent of NinjaCat, a Solana memecoin that shares revenue with holders.

We begin with memecoins, speculative digital tokens often based on internet jokes or personalities.

The memecoin launch platform Pump.fun is facing criticism online after figures circulated suggesting its most active token creators have earned large sums while most tokens lose nearly all their value. According to the figures, shared by several crypto commentators, the top twenty-five creators launched about seven hundred and seventy thousand tokens and earned roughly one hundred and twenty-eight million dollars. Only six of those tokens reached a market value of twenty million dollars. Some users are calling for a boycott. A widely shared quote attributing the criticism to Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin could not be traced to any original statement.

Pump.fun also announced a change to how new tokens trade. Creators can now pair a new token against any token already launched on the platform, rather than only a short list of approved assets. The company says purchases of a new token will be routed through the token it is paired with, adding demand for that token. Pump.fun's own token, PUMP, was down about eleven per cent over the past day, according to CoinGecko.

Trading data show the extreme volatility of newly created tokens on the Solana blockchain. According to the market-data site GeckoTerminal, a token called TikTok, created just before noon Pacific time today, has risen more than sixteen hundred per cent, to a market value of about six hundred and eighty thousand dollars. Another, BORDR, is up about seventeen hundred per cent. A third, swordinu, traded about five million dollars' worth in a day and has lost ninety-nine point nine per cent of its value. Separately, a token called TWEETCRAFT doubled in price after dozens of accounts posted near-identical promotional messages, a pattern often associated with co-ordinated promotion.

Two security incidents are drawing attention. A cryptocurrency trader known online as Frogman says about four million dollars was taken from two of his digital wallets in the early morning during the TOKEN2049 industry conference in Singapore. He says the funds were then moved through privacy services that make them harder to trace. Separately, on the BNB Chain network, an administrator account for a project called 79thVault used special permissions to withdraw about twelve and a half million dollars from a trading pool. A trader known as AguilaTrades has placed a forty-times-leveraged bet on Bitcoin that would be forcibly closed near eighty-one thousand five hundred dollars. Bitcoin is currently near {{BTC_PRICE}} dollars.

Turning now to the wider cryptocurrency market.

As of {{PRICES_AS_OF_SPOKEN}}, Bitcoin was near {{BTC_PRICE}} U.S. dollars, {{BTC_CHANGE_SPOKEN}} over twenty-four hours. Ether was near {{ETH_PRICE}} dollars, {{ETH_CHANGE_SPOKEN}}, and Solana near {{SOL_PRICE}}, {{SOL_CHANGE_SPOKEN}}. More than a billion dollars in leveraged trades were forcibly closed earlier today.

It was the largest single day of withdrawals in months.

The European Union's markets regulator has told licensed crypto firms to phase out stablecoins that do not meet EU rules, including Tether's USDT, by January eighth, twenty twenty-seven.

The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is proceeding with its own crypto trading rules while legislation stalls in Congress.

Strategy now holds a record eight hundred and forty-eight thousand bitcoin, and Cardone Capital bought forty more today.

Finally, a look at the themes shaping speculative trading this week.

Tokens based on AI-generated characters, including Frank Ashford and Jean Phil, are among the most actively traded on Solana this week.

Tokens linked to company shares are gaining attention. Base network lead Jesse Pollak called tokenized shares the industry's next major growth area.

A Citrini Research report on AI agents and crypto helped lift Derive's token about twenty-four per cent today.

Injective's community fund bought ten per cent of NinjaCat, a Solana memecoin that shares revenue with holders.
